title: C# multi-targeted down to net452 / netstandard2.0 (Transloadit Sharp)

versions.latest: C# 14 (released November 2025, default for net10.0); per-TFM defaults: .NET Framework all and netstandard2.0 = C# 7.3, net5.0 = 9, net6.0 = 10, net7.0 = 11, net8.0 = 12

versions.pinnedIn: not pinned: no global.json, so the highest installed SDK is used

rules.rule: Before calling any BCL API in src/Transloadit, check that its 'Applies to' list covers .NET Framework 4.5.2 and .NET Standard 2.0; if it does not, bridge it with an internal helper in src/Transloadit/Polyfills/ behind an exact TFM symbol, the way DateTimeOffsetExtensions does for net452.
rules.why: The library compiles the same source for 12 TFMs; an API that exists on net10.0 but not on net452/netstandard2.0 fails that inner build and blocks pack and deploy. Easy-to-miss examples: Array.Empty<T>() and Task.CompletedTask start at .NET Framework 4.6 (absent on net452); CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals exists only on .NET Core 2.1+/.NET Standard 2.1 (absent on every netfx TFM and netstandard2.0). IDE code fixes offered while editing in the net10.0 context suggest these newer APIs.
rules.repoConvention: Sound: gaps are bridged by internal extension methods in src/Transloadit/Polyfills/ guarded by the exact TFM symbol (#if NET452), and the consuming file adds the using under the same #if. This is the documented way to reach down-level frameworks (supply the missing API from a library), it keeps the helper out of the public surface, and it compiles to nothing on TFMs that have the real API.

rules.rule: Documented practice: do not set LangVersion above the default of the TFM being compiled. Microsoft states that using a C# version newer than the one associated with the target TFM is unsupported and can cause hard-to-diagnose compile-time and runtime errors; the defaults are C# 7.3 for every .NET Framework TFM and netstandard2.0, 9 for net5.0, 10 for net6.0, 11 for net7.0 and 12 for net8.0. While the repo keeps LangVersion 12, new code may rely only on features whose compiled form needs no type or runtime capability missing on net452/netstandard2.0 (pure syntax the compiler lowers to IL that runs on the .NET Framework 4.5.2 CLR, proven by the net452 and netstandard2.0 inner builds and by tests on a .NET Framework TFM). Never use: index/range operators (System.Index/System.Range), default interface members (.NET Core 3.0 CLR), init accessors and records (IsExternalInit), required members, UTF-8 string literals (ReadOnlySpan<byte>), System.Threading.Lock (C# 13), inline arrays or anything else the compiler binds to a library type.
rules.why: Above-default language versions are outside Microsoft's support matrix: a feature that looks like syntax may bind to a library type or depend on runtime behaviour absent on the old TFM, failing the inner build or, worse, misbehaving only on .NET Framework at run time. The repo's .editorconfig actively suggests several unsafe features (prefer_index_operator, prefer_range_operator, prefer_utf8_string_literals, prefer_system_threading_lock), so accepting an IDE suggestion is the usual way the break arrives.
where: .editorconfig csharp_style_prefer_index_operator / csharp_style_prefer_range_operator / csharp_style_prefer_utf8_string_literals / csharp_prefer_system_threading_lock / csharp_style_namespace_declarations = file_scoped:error
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: both csproj files set <LangVersion>12</LangVersion> for every TFM, which is above the documented default (C# 7.3) for net452, net461, net462, net472, net48 and netstandard2.0 and above the defaults for net5.0/net6.0/net7.0; existing shared source already uses C# 8-12 syntax (file-scoped namespaces, switch expressions, ??=, using declarations, collection expressions such as `parameters ??= []` in SmartCdnService). Fix: choose one supported configuration: (a) remove <LangVersion> so each TFM uses its default, which limits source shared with .NET Framework/netstandard2.0 to C# 7.3 and requires rewriting the newer syntax and .editorconfig preferences; or (b) narrow the TFM list so the oldest remaining target's default covers the syntax in use. Until decided, apply the 'may rely only on' list above and turn off the .editorconfig suggestions for library-dependent features.
rules.since: C# 8 (index/range, default interface members), C# 9 (init, records), C# 11 (required, u8 literals), C# 12 (inline arrays), C# 13 (Lock)

rules.rule: If a compiler-required type (IsExternalInit, RequiredMemberAttribute and similar) must be polyfilled, declare it internal and only for the TFMs that lack it, or type-forward it to the framework type on the TFMs that have it; never ship a public copy.
rules.why: init setters carry a modreq to IsExternalInit. When a netstandard2.0 consumer compiled against the polyfilled type runs against this package's net8.0+ build, the setter signature points at a different type and the call fails with MissingMethodException at run time. An internal copy also interacts with InternalsVisibleTo("Transloadit.Tests").

rules.rule: Guard TFM-specific code with the SDK's preprocessor symbols and pick the right family: NETFRAMEWORK / NET452 for .NET Framework, NETCOREAPP2_1_OR_GREATER or NET5_0_OR_GREATER for modern .NET, NETSTANDARD2_0 for the netstandard build. Keep the custom TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT constant defined identically in the library and the test project.
rules.why: NETSTANDARD2_0_OR_GREATER is defined only when the netstandard target itself is compiled, not for net4x or net5+ that implement it, so '#if NETSTANDARD2_0_OR_GREATER' silently drops code from 11 of the 12 builds. A TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT mismatch between the two csproj files makes the tests exercise the wrong serializer engine for a TFM.

rules.rule: Compare a computed HMAC with a caller-supplied signature in constant time: decode both to bytes and use CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals under #if NETCOREAPP2_1_OR_GREATER, and an internal polyfill elsewhere that XOR-accumulates every byte, returns early only on a length mismatch, and is marked [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.NoInlining | MethodImplOptions.NoOptimization)] as the runtime's own implementation is. Never compare signatures, tokens or secrets with ==, string.Equals or SequenceEqual.
rules.why: Consumers pass internet-originated webhook bodies and signatures to ValidateSignature. Ordinary equality is not designed to be timing-independent; FixedTimeEquals exists precisely so the comparison time does not depend on how many leading bytes match. A timing difference lets an attacker who can submit many forged notifications learn the expected signature byte by byte (auth bypass on the consumer's webhook endpoint). FixedTimeEquals is unavailable on net452..net48 and netstandard2.0, so the polyfill is mandatory there.
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: SignatureUtilities.ValidateSignature compares the expected and supplied hex strings with == in both the prefixed (sha256/sha384) and legacy sha1 branches. Fix: hex-decode both sides (reject malformed hex as a mismatch) and compare with FixedTimeEquals on NETCOREAPP2_1_OR_GREATER and an internal Polyfills/FixedTime helper elsewhere; add tests for equal-length mismatches, length mismatches and upper-case hex.

rules.rule: In src/Transloadit, append .ConfigureAwait(false) to every await, and never block on a Task (.Result, .Wait(), GetAwaiter().GetResult()). In test methods, do not call ConfigureAwait.
rules.why: The library runs inside arbitrary consumer contexts (WinForms/WPF, classic ASP.NET). Without ConfigureAwait(false) continuations are posted back to the caller's context, which costs throughput and deadlocks a caller that blocks on the returned task. ConfigureAwait(false) only helps when every await in the chain has it: an await on an already-completed task keeps running on the original context, so one missing call is enough to re-introduce the deadlock. In xUnit tests the opposite holds: ConfigureAwait(false) moves test code off xUnit's own limited pool onto the unbounded thread pool and defeats its parallelism limit (xUnit1030).
rules.repoConvention: Sound: CA2007 is error for src and silent for tests, and test code awaits without ConfigureAwait. This matches CA2007's own guidance (intended for libraries, suppress for application code) and xUnit's rule xUnit1030 (do not call ConfigureAwait in test methods).

rules.rule: Enforce analyzers on every build and every TFM: set <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild> so the IDExxxx severities in .editorconfig are applied by `dotnet build` and CI, and set <EnableNETAnalyzers>true</EnableNETAnalyzers> so the CA rules (including CA2007 at error) also run in the .NET Framework and netstandard2.0 inner builds. Until both are set, review code under #if TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT / #if NET452 and IDE-rule compliance by hand.
rules.why: Code-style (IDE) analysis is disabled by default for command-line builds, so .editorconfig entries marked :error or :warning only show in the editor and CI accepts violations. CA analysis is enabled by default only for .NET 5+ targets; code compiled only for net452/net461 (the Newtonsoft engine and the net452 polyfill) is never checked, so a missing ConfigureAwait or a stack-losing `throw ex;` there passes CI.
where: .editorconfig csharp_style_namespace_declarations = file_scoped:error; dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0060.severity = error; csharp_style_var_* = true:warning

src/Transloadit/Serialization/NewtonsoftJsonSerializer.cs, TransloaditContractResolver.cs, AnyOfConverter.cs, BooleanToIntConverter.cs, DateTimeConverters.cs, TransloaditSerializerSettings.cs (#if TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT)
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: .editorconfig declares IDE rules at error/warning but neither csproj nor Directory.Build.props sets EnforceCodeStyleInBuild, and EnableNETAnalyzers is not set, so CA rules run only in the net5.0+ inner builds. Fix: add both properties (Directory.Build.props or Transloadit.csproj), build once with TreatWarningsAsErrors to surface existing violations, and fix or explicitly re-scope them.

rules.rule: Treat every public member as a binary contract, and expose cancellation the TAP way: add a new overload taking `CancellationToken cancellationToken` and keep the old signature delegating to it with CancellationToken.None; never add an optional parameter to, rename a parameter of, or change the type of an existing public member.
rules.why: Consumers and other NuGet libraries compiled against an earlier Transloadit version call the exact old signature; adding a parameter, even an optional one, changes the IL signature and those callers fail with MissingMethodException until they recompile. Renaming a parameter breaks callers that use named arguments. Without a token, a consumer cannot abandon a slow upload or status poll except by disposing the shared HttpClient.
where: src/Transloadit/TransloaditClient.cs SendRequest<T> (both overloads, no CancellationToken today)
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: no public async method accepts a CancellationToken (the only token in src is AssemblyTracker's internal timeout CTS), although TAP guidance says to consider one. Fix: add `..., CancellationToken cancellationToken` overloads to SendRequest<T>, every service *Async method and WaitCompletionAsync, pass the token to HttpClient.SendAsync and Task.Delay, and keep the existing signatures as forwarding overloads.

rules.rule: Validate every reference argument of a public member at entry with ArgumentNullException via a throw expression (x ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(x))); ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull and the other static throw helpers are not available on the net452/netstandard2.0 builds.
rules.why: A public method that dereferences a null argument throws NullReferenceException, a reserved exception type that tells the caller nothing and that a consumer cannot distinguish from a bug in the library; storing a null dependency defers the failure far from the bad call. The static throw helpers the docs and IDE recommend do not compile on the old TFMs.
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation (partial): TransloaditClient's constructors validate with `?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(...))`, but SignatureService(secret), SmartCdnService(key, secret), AssemblyTracker(client) and SignatureUtilities.ValidateSignature(input, key, signature) accept nulls and fail later with NullReferenceException. Fix: add the same throw-expression checks (for ValidateSignature, decide between ArgumentNullException and returning false, see questions).

rules.rule: Never put `?` on a reference type: Nullable is disabled, so `?` is allowed only on value types (int?, DateTime?).
rules.why: In a disabled nullable context a reference-type annotation raises CS8632, which TreatWarningsAsErrors turns into a build failure.
rules.repoConvention: Sound as a hard constraint: disable is the compiler default, and turning nullable on is a deliberate whole-codebase migration that changes the annotations every consumer sees, not something a single change may start. While it is off, mixing in `?` on reference types only produces CS8632 build errors. Enabling it is tracked in questions.

rules.rule: Give every public type and member, including each public constant, a /// doc comment (with <param>/<returns> on public methods). Do not suppress CS1591; for large constant lists, generate the one-line <summary> comments rather than disabling the warning.
rules.why: GenerateDocumentationFile makes the compiler report CS1591 for each undocumented public member and TreatWarningsAsErrors turns it into a build error on every TFM. A file-wide `#pragma warning disable 1591` also hides every future undocumented member added to that file, and consumers see no IntelliSense text for the suppressed members.
where: src/Transloadit/Constants/Fonts.cs (`#pragma warning disable 1591` at line 1, never restored)
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: src/Transloadit/Constants/Fonts.cs starts with `#pragma warning disable 1591` and never restores it, so its public `const string` font names have no doc comments; the CS1591 reference names adding the comments as the good practice. Fix: generate a one-line `/// <summary>` per constant (for example the font's display name) and delete the pragma. Comment style elsewhere is sound: prose comments start lower-case without a trailing period (CLAUDE.md).

rules.rule: Format and parse every value that goes on the wire or into a signed string with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, and compare or sort protocol keys with StringComparison.Ordinal / StringComparer.Ordinal.
rules.why: Default overloads use the current culture of the consumer's thread: a de-DE decimal comma, a th-TH Buddhist-calendar year or a tr-TR dotless i changes the serialized value or the key order, so the API rejects the request or the server-side signature check fails.
where: src/Transloadit/Services/SmartCdnService.cs GetSignedSmartCdnUrl (StringComparer.Ordinal sort; signatureExpiration.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds().ToString() has no IFormatProvider, make it explicit with CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)
rules.repoConvention: Sound: serializers pass CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, SmartCdn sorts with StringComparer.Ordinal, and CultureRobustnessTests guards it under tr-TR, th-TH, ar-SA, fa-IR and de-DE, exactly as CA1305 and the string best-practices guide prescribe for data read by software. The one implicit-culture ToString() in SmartCdnService should be made explicit.

rules.rule: Use long-lived, shared HttpClient instances: when the caller supplies none, fall back to one static HttpClient (on NETCOREAPP2_1_OR_GREATER built on SocketsHttpHandler with PooledConnectionLifetime set, e.g. a few minutes) instead of a new HttpClient per TransloaditClient; never create an HttpClient per request; never dispose an HttpClient that came from TransloaditClientOptions.HttpClient; document that consumers should reuse one TransloaditClient or pass a shared/IHttpClientFactory client (the documented choice on .NET Framework).
rules.why: Each HttpClient that owns its handler has its own connection pool; creating and discarding them per call leaves sockets in TIME_WAIT and exhausts ports under load, especially on .NET Framework. A long-lived client without PooledConnectionLifetime resolves DNS only when a connection is created, so it keeps talking to a stale address after api2.transloadit.com moves. Disposing an injected client tears down a pool the consumer still uses.
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: MergeOptions creates `new HttpClient()` with the default handler for every TransloaditClient constructed without options.HttpClient, so consumers that create a TransloaditClient per request get one connection pool per request, and long-lived ones never set PooledConnectionLifetime. Fix: replace the fallback with a lazily created static HttpClient (SocketsHttpHandler + PooledConnectionLifetime under NETCOREAPP2_1_OR_GREATER, HttpClientHandler elsewhere), set the Transloadit-Client header per request instead of mutating DefaultRequestHeaders of a shared client, and document client reuse in readme.md.

rules.rule: Strong-name the assembly on every TFM (the library targets .NET Framework and .NET Standard), with the key pair checked into source control (or the public key plus public signing for regular builds), and InternalsVisibleTo naming the test assembly's full public key. Once a strong-named version has shipped, never add, remove or change the key.
rules.why: On .NET Framework strong naming is viral: a strong-named consumer can reference only strong-named assemblies, so an unsigned package cannot be used by those apps. Adding, removing or changing the key changes the assembly identity, which breaks every compiled consumer (binary break), so the decision has to be made once and versioned.
where: src/Transloadit/Transloadit.csproj <SignAssembly>True</SignAssembly> (no AssemblyOriginatorKeyFile, no .snk in the repo)
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation (suspected): SignAssembly=True is set but no key file exists in the repo and InternalsVisibleTo carries no public key, which indicates the shipped DLL is not actually strong-named, while CLAUDE.md says it is. Fix: check the public key token of the published 0.11.0 DLL. If it is signed, commit that key pair (or the public key with PublicSign) and add the PublicKey to InternalsVisibleTo. If it is unsigned, adding a key now is an identity change: do it only in a major version with a release note, or remove SignAssembly and the CLAUDE.md claim.

rules.rule: Pin the SDK with a global.json at the repo root (for example version 10.0.403 with rollForward latestFeature, allowPrerelease false), and treat NuGet audit warnings NU1901-NU1904 explicitly: WarningsNotAsErrors for normal builds, errors in a dedicated audit job.
rules.why: With no global.json the highest installed SDK is used, including previews outside Visual Studio; new SDKs bring new analyzer rules (AnalysisLevel defaults to latest) and warning waves that TreatWarningsAsErrors turns into errors. Because net10.0 is one of the TFMs, NuGetAuditMode defaults to 'all' for every TFM, so a newly published advisory against any transitive package fails the library build and the deploy workflow without a code change.
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: the repo has no global.json and no WarningsNotAsErrors for NU1901-NU1904, so local builds and CI use whichever SDK is newest on the machine. Fix: add global.json (10.0.403, rollForward latestFeature, allowPrerelease false), add `<WarningsNotAsErrors>$(WarningsNotAsErrors);NU1901;NU1902;NU1903;NU1904</WarningsNotAsErrors>` with an audit job that promotes them to errors, and let setup-dotnet read global.json.

bugCategories.name: tfm-api-gap
bugCategories.lookFor: New BCL calls, overloads or types in src/Transloadit that are absent on net452 (anything introduced in .NET Framework 4.6+, e.g. Array.Empty, Task.CompletedTask) or netstandard2.0 (CryptographicOperations, ThrowIfNull helpers, Span-based overloads); language features that need System.Index/Range, IsExternalInit or Lock; a polyfill guarded by the wrong symbol family.
bugCategories.failure: One inner build fails (CS0117/CS0246/CS0518) so `dotnet build`/`dotnet pack` fails for the whole package; a wrong #if silently removes code from some TFMs.

bugCategories.name: timing-unsafe-secret-compare
bugCategories.lookFor: ==, string.Equals, SequenceEqual or early-return loops comparing an HMAC, signature, token or secret with caller input.
bugCategories.failure: Comparison time leaks how many leading bytes match; an attacker can forge a valid webhook signature by timing many attempts (consumer-side auth bypass).

bugCategories.name: null-at-public-boundary
bugCategories.lookFor: Public methods or constructors that dereference a reference parameter (Split, Length, member access) without an ArgumentNullException check, or that store a null secret/client and fail later.
bugCategories.failure: NullReferenceException (a reserved exception type) from inside the library, e.g. ValidateSignature(input, key, null) when a webhook arrives without a signature field; or a deferred failure far from the bad call.

bugCategories.name: value-type-default-as-unset
bugCategories.lookFor: `options?.ValueTypeProperty ?? fallback` or `x?.Count ?? n` used to apply a default: the `??` only fires when the containing object is null, not when a caller-supplied object leaves an int/bool/TimeSpan property at its default.
bugCategories.failure: A caller passes `new AssemblyTrackerOptions()` without setting WaitCompletionTimeout; MergeOptions keeps 0, `new CancellationTokenSource(0)` expires immediately and WaitCompletionAsync throws TaskCanceledException on the first poll.

bugCategories.name: swallowed-or-reshaped-exception
bugCategories.lookFor: catch (Exception) or bare catch that returns default/false/null or only logs; `throw ex;` instead of `throw;`; catching TaskCanceledException instead of OperationCanceledException; changing which exception type an existing public method throws.
bugCategories.failure: Real failures (network, auth, malformed response) surface as 'no result' and the caller acts on missing data; stack traces are lost; a new exception type thrown from an existing code path breaks consumer catch blocks (disallowed behavioural break).

bugCategories.name: context-capture-deadlock
bugCategories.lookFor: An await in src/Transloadit without .ConfigureAwait(false) (especially in #if TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT/NET452 code that CA2007 never sees), or any .Result/.Wait()/GetAwaiter().GetResult() on a library task.
bugCategories.failure: A WinForms/WPF or classic ASP.NET consumer that blocks on the returned task hangs forever; others pay a context switch per await.

bugCategories.name: public-api-binary-break
bugCategories.lookFor: Diff of public signatures: added/removed/reordered parameters (including new optional ones), renamed parameters, changed return/property types, changed defaults, sealed types, removed members, new abstract members, a new or removed strong-name key.
bugCategories.failure: Applications that update the Transloadit package without recompiling every dependent library throw MissingMethodException/TypeLoadException at run time; named-argument callers stop compiling.

bugCategories.name: culture-sensitive-wire-value
bugCategories.lookFor: ToString(), Parse, string.Format, interpolation, ToLower/ToUpper, OrderBy or Compare on values that are serialized, signed or matched against API keys, without InvariantCulture or an Ordinal comparer.
bugCategories.failure: Under consumer locales such as tr-TR, de-DE, th-TH or fa-IR the request body, query string or string-to-sign differs, producing API validation errors or signature mismatches that never reproduce on an en-US machine.

bugCategories.name: conditional-compilation-drift
bugCategories.lookFor: A change applied to only one branch of `#if TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT` / `#else`, or a TFM added to one csproj condition list (System.Text.Json reference, DefineConstants, CsCheck version) but not the matching list in the other file.
bugCategories.failure: net452/net461 consumers (Newtonsoft engine) get different JSON than every other TFM, and CI never notices because net461 is not in the CI test matrix.

bugCategories.name: httpclient-per-call
bugCategories.lookFor: `new HttpClient()` or `new TransloaditClient(...)` without a supplied HttpClient inside loops, per-request handlers or short-lived objects; `using` around an injected HttpClient; long-lived clients without PooledConnectionLifetime on .NET Core/5+.
bugCategories.failure: Port exhaustion (SocketException) under load, stale DNS for long-lived clients, or ObjectDisposedException for the consumer's shared client.

testing.layers: Language-level behaviour (API availability, culture, signature comparison, null handling, serializer-engine parity) is proven by offline unit tests in tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/Unit and Tests/Models, run on more than one TFM: at least one modern TFM (net8.0+), one .NET Framework TFM (net48) and net461, which is the only test TFM that compiles TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT. net452 has no test TFM, so the library build for net452 is the only check there. Tests/Api/* are live integration tests and prove nothing language-specific.
testing.mutation: No mutation tool is configured. Signature comparison and culture handling are the highest-value targets if one is added (tooling pack decision).
traps: The CI matrix (.github/workflows/tests.yml) runs net8.0, net9.0, net10.0, net462, net472 and net48 only: net461 (the Newtonsoft engine), net6.0 and net7.0 are never tested in CI, and net452 is only built. Run -f net461 locally for any change touching serialization or #if branches.
CultureRobustnessTests swaps Thread.CurrentCulture; that is safe only because parallelization is disabled globally. A new test that changes ambient culture must restore it in finally.

Add constant-time and null/malformed-signature cases next to SignatureUtilitiesTests (null signature, unknown prefix, wrong length, upper-case hex) when changing ValidateSignature; the property tests do not cover malformed inputs.
Do not add ConfigureAwait in test methods (xUnit1030); tests/.editorconfig silences CA2007 for that reason.
Tests/Api/* need appsettings.Tests.json; filter to Tests.Unit/Tests.Models for language-level verification.

performance.note: Reuse HttpClient instances: each owns a connection pool, and per-call clients cost a new TCP/TLS handshake each time and can exhaust ports. On .NET Core/5+ a long-lived client should set PooledConnectionLifetime to pick up DNS changes; on .NET Framework IHttpClientFactory is the recommended way to manage clients.
ConfigureAwait(false) in library code also avoids posting every continuation back to the caller's synchronization context, which is measurable on UI threads.

security.note: ValidateSignature is the trust boundary for consumers' webhook endpoints (exposure: public, stakes: auth). Its comparison must be constant-time on all 12 TFMs (FixedTimeEquals where available, a NoInlining|NoOptimization XOR-accumulate polyfill elsewhere). Today it uses ==.

ValidateSignature throws ArgumentException for an unknown algorithm prefix and NullReferenceException for a null signature, both driven by attacker-controlled input, so a webhook handler without its own try/catch returns 500 instead of rejecting the request. Returning false instead counts as 'removing an exception to enable more robust behavior', which the compatibility rules allow, but it is still a behaviour change to decide and document.

Never set ServicePointManager.SecurityProtocol (or pass explicit SslProtocols) in the library. TLS defaults are decided by the consuming app's target framework: apps targeting .NET Framework 4.5.2 default SchUseStrongCrypto to 0 and apps targeting 4.6.1 or earlier default SystemDefaultTlsVersions to 0, so net452/net461 consumers may need the registry keys or AppContext switches. Document this instead of overriding the process-wide setting.

Package pins sit exactly on the patched floor of known advisories: Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.1 fixes GHSA-5crp-9r3c-p9vr (deeply nested JSON DoS, CVE-2024-21907) and System.Text.Json 8.0.5 fixes GHSA-8g4q-xg66-9fp4 ([JsonExtensionData] DoS, CVE-2024-43485; the library has no [JsonExtensionData] members). Never downgrade either, and keep NuGet audit running.

pins: LangVersion 12: src/Transloadit/Transloadit.csproj and tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj (above the documented default for net452..net48, netstandard2.0, net5.0-net7.0; see the LangVersion rule)
.NET SDK: unpinned (no global.json, to be added); local 10.0.403; CI installs 8.0.x/9.0.x/10.0.x per job
System.Text.Json 8.0.5 (library netstandard2.0, net462, net472, net48, net5.0, net6.0, net7.0); latest stable 10.0.14 still ships net462 and netstandard2.0 assets
tests: xunit 2.5.3, xunit.runner.visualstudio 2.5.3 / 2.4.3 (net461), Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 17.8.0, coverlet.collector 6.0.0, CsCheck 4.7.0 (net8.0+) / 2.9.0 (older)
lockStep: TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT DefineConstants and the Newtonsoft/System.Text.Json TFM condition lists in src/Transloadit/Transloadit.csproj with the net461 DefineConstants in tests/Transloadit.Tests/Transloadit.Tests.csproj
LangVersion in both csproj files, together with the oldest TFM in TargetFrameworks (its default language version is the supported ceiling)
TargetFrameworks in the library and the CI matrix in .github/workflows/tests.yml (a TFM missing from the matrix is untested)
global.json SDK version (once added) with the setup-dotnet versions in .github/workflows/tests.yml and deploy.yml
System.Text.Json version and the set of TFMs that reference it (moving off 8.x changes the minimum TFM set: STJ 8+ needs net462+)

deprecationsInUse: Out-of-support target frameworks still built: net452 and net461 (retired 2022-04-26), net5.0, net6.0, net7.0 (out of support); CheckEolTargetFramework=false in src/Transloadit/Transloadit.csproj suppresses NETSDK1138 for the .NET ones. net8.0 and net9.0 reach end of support on 2026-11-10 and net462 on 2027-01-13.
System.Text.Json 8.0.5 is the .NET 8 servicing line, which stops receiving fixes when .NET 8 support ends on 2026-11-10.
LangVersion 12 applied to TFMs whose documented default is lower (C# 7.3 for all .NET Framework TFMs and netstandard2.0): an unsupported configuration per Microsoft's language-versioning docs.

API 'Applies to' pages for ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull, Convert.ToHexString and HMAC static HashData were not fetched; the pack therefore names them only as helpers the docs recommend, not with exact first versions.
questions: Timing-safe comparison: SignatureUtilities.ValidateSignature compares signatures with ==. The rulebook now requires a constant-time byte comparison (FixedTimeEquals on NETCOREAPP2_1_OR_GREATER, internal polyfill on net452..net48 and netstandard2.0); schedule the fix? It is internal, with no public API impact.

Should ValidateSignature return false instead of throwing for a null signature (today NullReferenceException) or an unknown algorithm prefix (today ArgumentException, asserted by SignatureUtilitiesTests.ValidateSignature_UnknownPrefix_Throws)? The compatibility rules allow removing an exception for more robust behaviour, but consumers that catch ArgumentException would see a change.

Strong naming: Transloadit.csproj sets SignAssembly=True but no AssemblyOriginatorKeyFile exists and InternalsVisibleTo("Transloadit.Tests") carries no public key, which suggests the shipped DLL is not actually strong-named, while CLAUDE.md says it is. The rulebook now states the documented practice (strong-name on all TFMs, key in source control, never change it once shipped). Which fix applies: commit the existing key, add one in a major version, or drop SignAssembly and the CLAUDE.md claim? Check the public key token of the published 0.11.0 DLL first.

LangVersion 12 on net452..net48, netstandard2.0 (documented default C# 7.3) and net5.0-net7.0 is a configuration Microsoft calls unsupported. The rulebook now states that as the documented position and lists what new code may rely on meanwhile. Which fix: (a) drop <LangVersion> and rewrite shared source to C# 7.3, or (b) raise the oldest TFMs so their default covers the syntax in use? Or explicitly accept the deviation?
Add global.json (10.0.403, rollForward latestFeature, allowPrerelease false) and WarningsNotAsErrors for NU1901-NU1904 with a separate audit job, as the rulebook now requires?

Set EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true and EnableNETAnalyzers=true (rulebook best practice) so .editorconfig IDE severities and CA rules apply to CLI/CI builds and to the net452/net461/netstandard2.0 inner builds? Expect a one-time batch of existing violations.
Fonts.cs suppresses CS1591 for the whole file. Generate one-line /// summaries for the font constants and remove the pragma?
Add CancellationToken overloads to SendRequest<T>, every service *Async method and AssemblyTracker.WaitCompletionAsync (new overloads only, keeping the existing signatures)?

Replace the per-TransloaditClient `new HttpClient()` fallback in MergeOptions with a shared static client (SocketsHttpHandler + PooledConnectionLifetime on modern .NET), and document client reuse in readme.md?

Add ArgumentNullException checks to SignatureService, SmartCdnService and AssemblyTracker constructors, matching TransloaditClient? This makes failures earlier and clearer; a null argument that used to fail later now fails at construction.

Nullable reference types stay disabled (hard constraint for now). Do you want a separate, planned migration to <Nullable>enable</Nullable>, which the .NET 6+ templates default to and which would annotate the public API for consumers?
The CI matrix skips net461 (the only test TFM that exercises the Newtonsoft engine), net6.0 and net7.0. Add net461 to the .NET Framework job?

CLAUDE.md says Newtonsoft.Json is the only runtime dependency and describes Newtonsoft as the default serializer, but Transloadit.csproj uses System.Text.Json 8.0.5 on every TFM except net452/net461. CLAUDE.md looks stale; update it?

Support horizon: .NET 8 and .NET 9 reach end of support on 2026-11-10 (System.Text.Json 8.0.x stops being serviced) and .NET Framework 4.6.2 on 2027-01-13; net452, net461 and net5.0-net7.0 are already out of support. Keep building all of them, and move System.Text.Json to the 10.0.x line (still ships net462 and netstandard2.0)?
